insights.title: Worsening efficiency despite faster average pace
insights.body: Avg pace improved (-62 sec/km) while efficiency declined (+1.30 ml/kg/km) and avg HR rose (+10 bpm), indicating the runner is working harder physiologically to maintain pace — likely due to accumulated fatigue or detraining from low volume.

insights.title: Cadence collapse in easy runs signals fatigue
insights.body: On 2026-09-01 (5.0 km @ 9:36/km, HR 140), cadence was only 138 spm — 11 spm below 3-month median (149) — and ground contact time spiked to 389 ms, matching the 2026-08-23 recovery run (385 ms). This suggests residual fatigue impairing stride mechanics even at low intensities.

insights.title: Zone 2 dominance vanished — now Zone 3-heavy with no Z5
insights.body: This month’s zone distribution (Z2=74%, Z3=19%) contrasts sharply with last month (Z1=43%, Z2=22%, Z3=26%) — indicating loss of true easy running (Z1) and a shift toward moderately stressful efforts without high-intensity stimulus, reducing both recovery and adaptation stimulus.

recommendations.action: Tuesday: 4.5 km Zone 1 run, HR ≤125 bpm, cadence ≥145 spm, stop if vertical oscill >8.2 cm or ground contact >310 ms
recommendations.reason: Restores foundational aerobic stimulus without stress; cadence and biomechanical thresholds act as real-time fatigue gates.

recommendations.action: Thursday: 20-min walk + 3x2-min barefoot strides on grass (focus on light footstrike and 160+ spm), no HR monitoring
recommendations.reason: Neuromuscular re-education without cardiovascular load; addresses cadence collapse and vertical oscill elevation seen in recent runs.

recommendations.action: Saturday: Complete 30 min of guided HRV breathing (e.g., Garmin Breathe app) at bedtime, preceded by 15 min screen-free wind-down
recommendations.reason: Compensates for missing HRV/sleep data by proactively supporting autonomic recovery — essential given compromised readiness status.
